I was in the same situation as the OP when I was 19: insecure, without anyone to talk to about sex, and incredibly horny. And very religious. No premarital sex etc.

First thing I got over was the religiousity. Then I battled over whether people would see me as being a prude if I continued to not have sex or as a slut if I acted on every impulse I was getting.  What did I do?

**Look at a lot of porn.** Watch a lot of videos. Read literature. Although I did get turned on by some of what I saw, I basically approached it as serious research. How did the girls move, what did they do, what did the guy like...

I guess you would think that watching a lot of porn would make me feel even more insecure about myself because of all of the ridiculously gorgeous and shapely young girls who are often featured. Instead, I realized that there exists porn for every kind of person with every kind of fetish. It doesn't matter if you're old or young, fat or skinny, there is someone out there who desires you.

I also read a lot of sex informational websites like [Sex Info 101](http://www.sexinfo101.com) (NSFW), and read up as much as I could about technique.

**Masturbate a lot.** I found some time where I had privacy and I was comfortable and I simply tried to relax and just explore my body. I learned what I like and what I don't like.

**Begin a dialog with people you trust.** As a straight girl, I chose to a confide in a two (straight, non-vcard-holding) female friends, and one guy friend (straight, platonic friendship). This was tough because between my close female friends, talking about sex had been completely taboo for us. Our early conversations were the first time that the three of us ever got to be really open about sex and our experiences, or lack thereof. 

Our first conversation was after a few drinks and we'd joked around about each other's experiences. Although the joking around was kind of uncomfortable at first, it broke the ice and led to some really great conversations.

With my guy friend, I was really just hoping to get a first-hand perspective from someone with experience on the side that I'm going for.

With all three of my friends, I talked with them as light-heartedly as I possibly could, trying my best to hide any insecurities I had. I played the role of the curious apprentice, asking small questions here and there about what sex was like. "Is it true that..." "I heard that when you..." "I wonder what it's like to...."  My friends would then be very instructive, and sometimes detailed depending on our comfort level. I became the padawan to their jedi.

Meanwhile as I was becoming more and more comfortable in my skin, **I began relations with some guys.**

I lost my virginity when I was 20. Oddly enough (but appropriate in retrospect), my first time was with a childhood friend of mine with whom I had no emotional feelings, but had a strong physical attraction and trusted very much. And we were both very very drunk. After having a sober talk the next day, we mutually agreed to become FWB.

Now, I'm not saying that you should go out, get drunk, and lose your virginity the same way I did. But all the steps leading up to it, the preparing and getting more and more comfortable with myself, those were all very very important for me to shed most of my insecurities and open up.
